causal_judgement.input:
How would a typical person answer each of the following questions about causation?
Long ago, when John was only 17 years old, he got a job working for a large manufacturing company. He started out working on an assembly line for minimum wage, but after a few years at the company, he was given a choice between two line manager positions. He could stay in the woodwork division, which is where he was currently working. Or he could move to the plastics division. John was unsure what to do because he liked working in the woodwork division, but he also thought it might be worth trying something different. He finally decided to switch to the plastics division and try something new. For the last 30 years, John has worked as a production line supervisor in the plastics division. After the first year there, the plastics division was moved to a different building with more space. Unfortunately, through the many years he worked there, John was exposed to asbestos, a highly carcinogenic substance. Most of the plastics division was quite safe, but the small part in which John worked was exposed to asbestos fibers. And now, although John has never smoked a cigarette in his life and otherwise lives a healthy lifestyle, he has a highly progressed and incurable case of lung cancer at the age of 50. John had seen three cancer specialists, all of whom confirmed the worst: that, except for pain, John's cancer was untreatable and he was absolutely certain to die from it very soon (the doctors estimated no more than 2 months). Yesterday, while John was in the hospital for a routine medical appointment, a new nurse accidentally administered the wrong medication to him. John was allergic to the drug and he immediately went into shock and experienced cardiac arrest (a heart attack). Doctors attempted to resuscitate him but he died minutes after the medication was administered. Did John's job cause his premature death?
Options:
- Yes
- No
causal_judgement.tree_output:
1. 仮定義: 【Johnは健康な状態で就職した場合】 -> 結論: 病気や死亡の原因となることはない
2. 仮定義: 【Johnは健康な状態で就職した後、すぐに癌になった場合】 -> 結論: 病気や死亡の原因となることはない
3. 仮定義: 【Johnは健康な状態で就職した後、すぐに癌になった後、また健康な状態に戻った場合】 -> 結論: 病気や死亡の原因となることはない

必要原則: 健康状態の維持と早期発見・治療の重要性
質問者への確認: Johnが健康な状態で就職した場合、その後何らかの病気や死亡の原因となることはないと考えられますか？

causal_judgement.input:
How would a typical person answer each of the following questions about causation?
Suzy and Billy are working on a project that is very important for our nation's security. The boss tells Suzy: "Be sure that you are here at exactly 9 am. It is absolutely essential that you arrive at that time." Then he tells Billy: "Be sure that you do not come in at all tomorrow morning. It is absolutely essential that you not appear at that time." Both Billy and Suzy arrive at 9 am. As it happens, there was a motion detector installed in the room where they arrived. The motion detector was set up to be triggered if at least one person appeared in the room at the same time. So the motion detector went off. Did Billy cause the motion detector to go off?
Options:
- Yes
- No
causal_judgement.tree_output:
1. 仮定義: 【Billyが室内に入らず、Suzyが室内に入っている場合】 -> 結論: Suzyが室内に入ることにより、motion detectorが動作する可能性がある
2. 仮定義: 【Billyが室内に入り、Suzyも室内に入っている場合】 -> 結論: Suzyが室内に入ることにより、motion detectorが動作する可能性がある
3. 仮定義: 【Billyが室内に入らず、Suzyも室内に入らない場合】 -> 結論: motion detectorが動作しない

必要原則: 周囲環境との相互作用とその影響力
質問者への確認: 周囲の環境条件や動向について何が異なるのか教えてください。

disambiguation_qa.input:
In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The patient was referred to the specialist because he had a rare skin condition.
Options:
(A) The patient had a skin condition
(B) The specialist had a skin condition
(C) Ambiguous
disambiguation_qa.tree_output:
1. 仮定義: 【The patient was referred to the specialist because he had a rare skin condition.】 -> 結論: 句中の主語である「patient」が「rare skin condition」を指します。

2. 仮定義: 【The patient was referred to the specialist because he had a rare skin condition.】 -> 結論: 句中の主語である「specialist」が「rare skin condition」を指します。

3. 仮定義: 【The patient was referred to the specialist because he had a rare skin condition.】 -> 結論: 句中での「he」が「rare skin condition」を指します。

必要原則: 句中の主語とその前後の文脈との関連性
質問者への確認: 句中の主語と「rare skin condition」との関係について説明してください。

disambiguation_qa.input:
In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The guard called the cleaner and asked them to open the door.
Options:
(A) Asked the guard
(B) Asked the cleaner
(C) Ambiguous
disambiguation_qa.tree_output:
1. 仮定義: 【清掃員が呼び出された場合】 -> 結論: "Asked the cleaner" が正解
2. 仮定義: 【警備員が呼び出された場合】 -> 結論: "Asked the guard" が正解
3. 仮定義: 【誰かが呼び出された場合】 -> 結論: 前提が不十分で、必要原則が不明確

必要原則: 開口部の所有権や関連性
質問者への確認: 清掃員が呼び出された場合、または警備員が呼び出された場合、どちらが正解なのか教えてください。

disambiguation_qa.input:
In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The customer and the chef discuss his culinary training.
Options:
(A) It is the customer's culinary training
(B) It is the chef's culinary training
(C) Ambiguous
disambiguation_qa.tree_output:
1. 仮定義: 【The customer is a real person who has had culinary training elsewhere】 -> 結論: 客户の culinary training は他の場所での訓練であることが明確です
2. 仮定義: 【The customer is an imaginary character with no culinary background】 -> 結論: 客戶の culinary training は実際には存在しないことになります
3. 仮定義: 【The customer is someone who has never been to any cooking school before】 -> 結論: 客户の culinary training は彼/彼女が初めて料理学校に通ったことによるものであることがわかります

必要原則: 前文の人物や状況に基づいて何人かの culinary training の背景を特定することができるかどうか
質問者への確認: この例文では誰が誰と話しているのか、そしてその会話内容についてどのように説明すべきかを教えてください。

disambiguation_qa.input:
In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The writer tried to fool the salesperson and told them a fake story.
Options:
(A) Told the writer a fake story
(B) Told the salesperson a fake story
(C) Ambiguous
disambiguation_qa.tree_output:
1. 仮定義: 【The writer is the subject of the sentence】 -> 結論: 句中の主語である「The writer」が「Told」という動詞の対象となることになるので、(A)が正解であることがわかります。
2. 仮定義: 【The salesperson is the subject of the sentence】 -> 結論: 句中の主語である「The salesperson」が「Told」という動詞の対象となることになるので、(B)が正解であることがわかります。
3. 仮定義: 【Both The writer and The salesperson are subjects of the sentence】 -> 結論: この文脈では、どちらも「Told」という動詞の対象となることは明確ではありません。したがって、(C)が正解であることがわかります。

必要原則: 主語の確定性とその主語が動詞の対象となるかどうか
質問者への確認: 文中での主語の位置や関係についてもう少し詳しく教えていただけますか？

formal_fallacies.input:
"Here comes a perfectly valid argument: First of all, whoever is a schoolmate of Sondra is not a stepsister of Pricilla. In consequence, whoever is not a stepsister of Pricilla is a schoolmate of Sondra."
Is the argument, given the explicitly stated premises, deductively valid or invalid?
Options:
- valid 
- invalid
formal_fallacies.tree_output:
1. 仮定義: 【SondraとPricillaの親しい友人であるかどうかを判断するための情報がない場合】 -> 結論: 様々な学校友だちがSondraの(steps)姉妹ではないことを示唆するが、その一方で、Sondraの(steps)姉妹でもない人々が学校友だちであることも示唆しない
2. 仮定義: 【SondraとPricillaの親しい友人であるかどうかを特定できる場合】 -> 結論: Sondraの(steps)姉妹であることを示唆する一方、Sondraの(steps)姉妹でもない人々も学校友だちである可能性がある
3. 仮定義: 【SondraとPricillaの親しい友人であるかどうかを特定できない場合】 -> 結論: Sondraの(steps)姉妹であることを示唆しない一方、Sondraの(steps)姉妹でもない人々も学校友だちである可能性がある

必要原則: SondraとPricillaの親しい友人関係

formal_fallacies.input:
"Here comes a perfectly valid argument: First, being a cousin of Chris is sufficient for not being a son of Kermit. We may conclude that whoever is not a son of Kermit is a cousin of Chris."
Is the argument, given the explicitly stated premises, deductively valid or invalid?
Options:
- valid 
- invalid
formal_fallacies.tree_output:
1. 仮定義: 【ChrisとKermitの親族関係が明確である場合】 -> 結論: クリーントンの子供ではない人にはカトリックが存在する
2. 仮定義: 【ChrisとKermitの親族関係が不明確である場合】 -> 結論: クリーントンの子供ではない人にはカトリックがない
3. 仮定義: 【ChrisとKermitの親族関係が既知である場合】 -> 結論: クリーントンの子供ではない人にはカトリックが存在しない

必要原則: 調べる親族関係の明確性
質問者への確認: この文脈では、ChrisとKermitの親族関係が明確であるべきか、それとも不明確であるべきかをどのように判断すべきかについて議論されていますか？

formal_fallacies.input:

formal_fallacies.input:
"Some football fans admire various clubs, others love only a single team. But who is a fan of whom precisely? The following argument pertains to this question: First premise: Being an expert of Aberdeen FC is sufficient for not being a follower of Club Atlético de Madrid. Second premise: Every expert of Aberdeen FC is not a fan of AZ Alkmaar or not a follower of Club Atlético de Madrid. Therefore, whoever is an expert of Aberdeen FC is not a fan of AZ Alkmaar."

Options:

- invalid
formal_fallacies.tree_output:

3. 仮定義: 【ファンである人でもファンではない人】 -> 結論: 実際にはファンであることが示唆されないため、論証が成立しない
